slot.brief: A rectangular cycle on a P–V diagram; find the net work done from the enclosed area.

stem: A gas follows the rectangular cycle shown on the $P$–$V$ diagram. What is the net work done on the gas in one cycle?

verdicts.working: The cycle is counterclockwise, so net work done by the gas is negative. The enclosed area is $(250-100)\,\text{kPa}\times(5-2)\,\text{L}=450\,\text{J}$, using $1\,\text{kPa·L}=1\,\text{J}$. Thus work done on the gas is $+450\,\text{J}$.

working:
$W_{\text{on}}=\Delta P\,\Delta V$
$=(250-100)(5-2)=450\ \text{kPa L}$
$1\ \text{kPa L}=1\ \text{J}$
$W_{\text{on}}=450\ \text{J}$

Independent check: The cycle is counterclockwise, so net work done by the gas is negative. The enclosed area is $(250-100)\,\text{kPa}\times(5-2)\,\text{L}=450\,\text{J}$, using $1\,\text{kPa·L}=1\,\text{J}$. Thus work done on the gas is $+450\,\text{J}$.
solution:
For a counterclockwise cycle, the net work done on the gas equals the area enclosed in the $P$–$V$ diagram.
$$W_{\text{on}}=(250-100)(5-2)=450\ \text{kPa·L}=450\ \text{J}$$

draft.stem: A gas follows the rectangular cycle shown on the $P$–$V$ diagram. What is the net work done on the gas in one cycle?

figure.description: Draw a $P$–$V$ graph with $V$ on the horizontal axis (in L) and $P$ on the vertical axis (in kPa). Mark vertical-axis levels $100$ and $250$, and horizontal-axis positions $2$ and $5$. Draw a rectangle with corners at $(2\text{ L},100\text{ kPa})$, $(2\text{ L},250\text{ kPa})$, $(5\text{ L},250\text{ kPa})$, and $(5\text{ L},100\text{ kPa})$. Add arrows around the rectangle in the order lower-left to lower-right to upper-right to upper-left and back to lower-left. Label the axes and their units.

draft.distractor_notes: B: uses the sign for work done by the gas. C: doubles the enclosed area. D: doubles the area and uses the wrong sign.
